topic: Pus swabs and antibiotics in abscess drainage

audits.title: EP.FRI.469 A closed-loop audit regarding the practice of sending Pus Swab for culture and sensitivity in Pilonidal abscess drainage
audits.setting: Barts Health NHS Trust; incision and drainage of pilonidal abscess

cycle1.result: Swabs sent in 77% of cases; average reporting time 4.3 days; 92% discharged on antibiotics; swab results did not alter management.

audits.intervention: Treatment protocol changed to stop routine swabs; multiple teaching sessions for trainees and education of theatre staff.
audits.other_findings: 250 patients in total across the study; the change was reported to give large cost savings.
audits.citation: Sarodaya V, Nasser M, Hussain M. EP.FRI.469 A closed-loop audit regarding the practice of sending Pus Swab for culture and sensitivity in Pilonidal abscess drainage. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab312.076.

audits.title: EP.FRI.535 A clinical audit of post-operative antibiotics prescription in uncomplicated perianal abscesses
audits.standard: ACPGBI guidelines: incision and drainage within 24 hours; antibiotics not indicated in routine uncomplicated perianal abscess
audits.setting: London university teaching hospital (Croydon University Hospital), emergency surgical admissions

cycle1.result: 15/36 received empirical post-operative antibiotics, with no clear indication in 60% of those; 86% had surgical drainage within 24 hours.

audits.other_findings: Most common agent was co-amoxiclav (53%), then co-amoxiclav with metronidazole (33%); one patient readmitted for second drainage at 3 months.
audits.citation: Zhao S, Najdawi A, Laliotis A, Thomas R, Boghdady M. EP.FRI.535 A clinical audit of post-operative antibiotics prescription in uncomplicated perianal abscesses. British Journal of Surgery. 2021;108(Supplement_7). doi:10.1093/bjs/znab312.089.

audits.title: SRS385 - Audit of routine pus swabbing in abscess drainage: are we following guidance?
audits.standard: Guidance recommending selective pus swabbing for recurrent, persistent or treatment-resistant abscesses
audits.setting: Emergency general surgery, Calderdale and Huddersfield NHS Trust

cycle1.result: Pus swabs taken in 76/122 (62.3%), with results acted on in only 5/76 (6.6%).

audits.other_findings: 30-day recurrence 3.9% swabbed vs 4.3% non-swabbed; discharge on antibiotics associated with recurrence (aOR 13.76, P = 0.004).
audits.citation: Boalot A, Hasan M, Younes A, Salih T. SRS385 - Audit of routine pus swabbing in abscess drainage: are we following guidance?. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_2). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag018.341.

audits.title: TPT 6.05 Breaking Routine Practice: Eliminating Unnecessary Pus Swabs and Antibiotic Use in Perianal Abscess Drainage — A Closed-Loop Audit Promoting Guideline Adherence
audits.standard: ACPGBI consensus guidance: no routine pus swabs or antibiotics in uncomplicated perianal abscess
audits.setting: Royal Wolverhampton NHS Trust, district general hospital

cycle1.result: Pus swabs taken in 70% (35/50); antibiotics given in 54% (27/50); only 6% (2/35) of cultures reviewed.

audits.intervention: Targeted education to the surgical team, theatre staff engagement and guideline distribution.
audits.other_findings: Antibiotic use without a clear indication remained unchanged.
audits.citation: Pulluru Rajasekhar D, Nagui N, Ryan B, Jarral H, Lopez T, Liu B. TPT 6.05 Breaking Routine Practice: Eliminating Unnecessary Pus Swabs and Antibiotic Use in Perianal Abscess Drainage — A Closed-Loop Audit Promoting Guideline Adherence. British Journal of Surgery. 2026;113(Supplement_8). doi:10.1093/bjs/znag087.228.

audits.title: Closing the Evidence-Practice Gap: A Quality Improvement Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing Following Incision and Drainage of Superficial Skin, Pilonidal and Perianal Abscesses.
audits.standard: Local antibiotic prescribing guideline after incision and drainage; target 70% compliance
audits.setting: St George Hospital, Sydney (metropolitan teaching hospital)
audits.intervention: Concise prescribing guideline disseminated by posters, email and an in-person departmental meeting
audits.other_findings: 70% target not reached; 35/59 (59.3%) still not guideline-concordant.
audits.citation: O'Malley FM, Bothe J. Closing the Evidence-Practice Gap: A Quality Improvement Audit of Antibiotic Prescribing Following Incision and Drainage of Superficial Skin, Pilonidal and Perianal Abscesses. Cureus. 2026;18(8):e115271. doi:10.7759/cureus.115271. PMID: 42801007.
